questions.q: Why did the 50-record bulk test from Lesson 10 pass even though the original `beforeInsert` logic wasn't actually bulk-safe at every volume?
options: Because the trigger handler was already fully refactored at that point
Because 50 queries is still under the 100-query synchronous governor limit, even though one query per record doesn't scale -- a larger volume like 200 would exceed that limit
Because Apex ignores governor limits during tests
Because the handler never actually queries anything
questions.explain: At 50 records, one query per record in the loop totals 50 queries -- within the 100-query limit -- which is why it passed despite not being a genuinely bulk-safe pattern; at 200 records it would exceed the limit.

questions.q: What is the specific refactor this lesson applies to make the claim coverage check bulk-safe?
options: Remove the coverage check entirely
Move the check to a nightly Batch Apex job instead of the trigger
Switch the query from SOQL to SOSL
Query once for the whole batch into a Map<Id, Service_Contract__c> keyed by Asset Id, then look up each claim's contract from the map inside the loop instead of querying per record
questions.explain: The fix is the standard query-outside-the-loop refactor: one batched query building a Map, then an in-memory lookup inside the loop rather than a query per record.

questions.q: Why does the Case to Installation Job Flow from Lesson 6 also need a performance review, per this lesson?
options: Because Flow cannot be bulkified under any circumstances
Because Flows are always slower than Apex regardless of design
Because a Get Records element can still issue its query per flow interview (per record) unless written with batch-aware patterns, the same per-record query risk as Apex
Because Flow does not support record-triggered automation
questions.explain: Even though the platform bulkifies Flow across records in one transaction, a Get Records element can still run once per interview/record, mirroring the same per-record query concern flagged in the trigger.

questions.q: What does this lesson recommend as the first step of a performance review, rather than reasoning about bulk safety in the abstract?
options: Deliberately bulk-loading realistic data volume into a scratch org and observing what actually breaks or slows down
Reading the Apex Developer Guide's governor limits page one more time
Rewriting all Apex classes from scratch
Disabling all triggers during the review
questions.explain: The lesson recommends actually loading realistic bulk volume and observing behavior, rather than only reasoning about correctness abstractly.

questions.q: Why does the performance review conclude `StaleInstallationJobBatch` from Lesson 11 is already structurally safe at any volume?
options: Because it never queries any data
Because it runs only once per year
Because it is written in a special bulk-only syntax unavailable to triggers
Because Batch Apex's chunking exists specifically to process large record sets across separate transactions, unlike a single synchronous transaction
questions.explain: Batch Apex's whole design splits work into chunks across transactions specifically to handle large volumes safely, which is why the review only checks its scope size rather than flagging a fundamental bulk-safety problem.
